title: Months, Adjectives and Agreement
welcome_lead: Apply your vocabulary: months, common adjectives and how they agree with nouns.
meta_desc: GCSE Spanish application adventure on months and adjective agreement.
final_note: ¡Muy bien! You can now describe things with confidence.

concepts.def: December — last month of the year.
Good — adjective that agrees in gender.
Big — same form for masculine and feminine.

walkthroughs.body_html: The twelve months: enero, febrero, marzo, abril, mayo, junio, julio, agosto, septiembre, octubre, noviembre, diciembre. They are not capitalised. To say 'in May' use en mayo.

Most Spanish adjectives change ending to match the noun. Un libro pequeño (small book, masc.) vs una casa pequeña (small house, fem.). Adjectives ending in -e like grande don't change: un libro grande, una casa grande.
In Spanish, descriptive adjectives usually come after the noun: un coche rojo (a red car), una flor bonita (a pretty flower). This is the opposite of English word order!
